newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Declared candidate for HK top job pulls out.
newsitem.headline: Declared candidate for HK top job pulls out.

text.p: Hong Kong lawyer Lo Tak-shing, the first declared candidate for the territory's leadership after its 1997 return to China, pulled out of the race on Thursday.
The British colony reverts to Beijing next July 1 and becomes a Special Administrative Region of communist China, led a Chief Executive to be elected this year by a 400-member body.

"When I first signalled my interest earlier this year, I made it clear that I would only enter the election if there were no other candidates who could carry out the responsibilities of the position," Lo said in a statement.
"Now, with the entry of a number of suitably qualified contenders, I see no further need to put myself forward."
Lo was the second declared candidate to bow out of the contest. Last week, former Hong Kong High Court judge Arthur Garcia also reversed a previous decision to stand for the post.
The latest withdrawal came just after the opening of the two-week official registration period for candidates.
Shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa and Chief Justice Sir Ti Liang Yang, two other hopefuls who have declared their interest in the job, have yet to submit formal bids.
Tung is seen as China's favourite to fill the post.
